{{Quote|If necessary, I can invoke Directive One-Oh-Three. ''[&hellip;]'' In the absence of orders to the contrary, all fleet officers&mdash;''"<br />"''I'm familiar with the directive.|Captains Calo Drusan and Voss Parck|<ref name="Choices">''[[Choices of One]]''</ref>}}
'''Directive One-Oh-Three''', which, in the absence of directives, [[Commanding officer/Legends|commanded]] all [[Officer/Legends|officers]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Imperial Navy/Legends|fleet]] to do something.<ref name="Choices" /> In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">The events of ''[[Choices of One]]'' take place in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] according to ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]].</ref> [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Nuso Esva|Odo]] of the [[Imperial Court/Legends|Imperial Court]]&mdash;who in fact was the [[Storm-hair|alien]] [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] Nuso Esva&mdash;told [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Voss Parck/Legends|Voss Parck]] of the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Admonitor]]'' to travel to the [[Candoras sector/Legends|Candoras sector's]] [[Poln system/Legends|Poln system]] immediately. However, Parck refused to do so, forcing Captain [[Calo Drusan]] of the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Chimaera/Legends|''Chimaera'']] to threaten the captain with invoking the directive. Although Parck stated that the ''Admonitor'' was detached from the Imperial fleet, the Empire contacted the ''Admonitor'' and verified Odo's request, forcing Parck to travel to the Poln [[Star system/Legends|system]]. Parck considered Directive One-Oh-Three unclear.<ref name="Choices" />

==Behind the scenes==
Directive One-Oh-Three was mentioned in [[Timothy Zahn]]'s [[2011]] novel ''[[Choices of One]]''.<ref name="Choices" />
